title: Officer Tago shares the latest HLP  update from Beat 3.
description:
🧹 Officer Tago shares the latest update on Homeless Outreach & Enforcement. From 30+ arrests to clearing 5,000 lbs of trash, the HLP team is working hard to improve quality of life across the city.

#SantaMonica #PublicSafety
transcript_text: Hello Santa Monica, Officer Tagaloa here, your B3 Neighborhood Resource Officer. During this reporting period, HOST stayed active across the city. They focused on our parks, downtown area, beach areas, and freeway underpasses. Wherever the issues we're servicing, that's where we focus our time. Consistent presence, no shortcuts. Officers made over 30 misdemeanor and felony arrests tied to public camping, parole violations, narcotic offenses, sex offender registration violations, and outstanding warrants. Many of these involved repeat behavior, so enforcement was necessary to address ongoing quality of life impacts in our public spaces. At the same time, we continue working closely with the Department of Mental Health, Santa Monica's HOST team, code enforcement, and our reach partners. When someone was open to services, we connected them. When the laws were being ignored, we took action. That balance is part of the job, but accountability is always clear. By the numbers, our HOST team responded to 255 radio calls, conducted 221 self-initiated contacts, addressed nine encampments, made 31 arrests, and conducted five mental health evaluations. An incident of note, near the I-10 at Lincoln, officers continued addressing freeway and bankment encampments. Working alongside HOST and Meripost Landscaping, over 5,000 lb of trash was removed. That's more than 2 and 1/2 tons cleared from one of the busiest gateways into our city, reducing fire hazards, improving visibility, and restoring that corridor for everyone who travels through it. We're going to keep addressing issues directly and staying consistent across the city. Steady, grounded, and focused. That work doesn't stop, and neither do we.
